scope: visual motion review for severe unintended translation, scale jumps and frame pops
reviewer: Codex final visual review with byte-identical prior coverage
methods: For all six changed arrow states, viewed every frame and explicit loop return in 48px and96px full-sequence boards on light and dark backgrounds (24 boards across the two original themes).

Loaded original two themes six changed arrow states at normal and quarter speed, at 48px and96px, in Chromium. Observed distinct live playback phases; exhaustive edge coverage derives from sequence boards.
Confirmed each enlarged operation symbol stays fixed while eye, muzzle, ears, chest and paw movements remain coherent; no severe unintended shift, scale pop, clipping or loop jump was observed.

Preserved prior complete visual approval for the other eleven states only after matching every exported PNG SHA256 at all five sizes against the previous reviewed output. These eleven states were not newly browser-reviewed for this arrow-only revision.
Native loading and automatic motion analysis were rerun on the final revision; heuristic results were context only.
repairs: Replaced six small operation arrows with common larger pixel symbols, using one shared pet transform per state.
remaining_limitations: Minor pixel-cluster/contour variation remains in fur, ears, paws and a few badge silhouettes; this is not a claim of perfectly identical stationary pixels.
Intentional blinking, ear/ruff movement, paw gestures, question-mark scaling and sleep/ZZZ changes remain visible.
Automatic body-registration is heuristic and is recorded as context only.
Actual desktop click feel, installation, cross-DPI and multi-monitor behavior are outside this visual review.
